identification: Mixed household lot of 5 items (description: PAIR TABLE LAMPS, PLANTER, COFFEE GRINDER ETC). (1) Pair of tall slim sage-green painted turned-timber column/candlestick table lamps with round stepped bases, cream candle-sleeve fittings and matching cream/blue-green sprig-pattern fabric shades. (2) Clover/trefoil-shaped olive-green painted metal planter with diamond lattice pierced sides; the photo suggests a second, smaller clover planter nested inside it, so possibly 2 planters. (3) Small wooden box-style hand coffee grinder with cast-iron decorative hopper cover and crank, brass cup/pan, and a single drawer with brass knob; stained timber, looks 20th century reproduction or late European style. (4) Large oval plywood-style tray with woven cane/wicker braided rim and a turned wooden knob handle visible. Generic decorative items, no maker identified.
marks_seen: Both photos viewed at full size and zoomed: grinder (hopper, cup, box sides, drawer knob), planter, tray, lamp bases, shades. No maker mark, stamp, name or patent text legible on any item. Only the lot tickets (599) are readable. Photo resolution is low (about 800x600 native), so marks on the underside of the grinder or tray base would not be visible anyway.
google_searches: Searched antique wooden box coffee grinder with cast iron hopper and brass cup (results were generic collector guides and Etsy/1stDibs listings, no result text on value). Did not search the lamps, planter or tray as they carry no marks. Nothing identifies a maker; grinder style is common (Zassenhaus/Peugeot/Kenrick type box mills are all similar), cannot attribute from the photo.

identification: Set of 6 high-back cane-panelled dining chairs (description: SET OF 6 CANE BACKED UPHOLSTERED DINING CHAIRS). Photo 1 shows all six (4 side chairs, 2 carvers with arms), photo 2 a carver close up, photo 3 a side chair. Late 20th century American/Asian-made colonial style (not antique).
